{"kind":"tool","id":"iBLPOSQGnP4","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"marketlab/src/components/ui/input.tsx","instructions":"Make Input follow changes to its value prop so a parent can reset it.","content":"import React, { useEffect, useState } from "react";

interface InputProps {
  type?: string;
  placeholder?: string;
  value?: string;
  onChange?: (value: string) => void;
  onSubmit?: (value: string) => void;
  disabled?: boolean;
  label?: string;
  className?: string;
}

/**
 * Text/number input.
 *
 * Editable locally (so typing never depends on a parent round-trip) but it
 * follows the `value` prop when the parent changes it — otherwise a parent that
 * clears or preselects a value would silently keep showing the stale text.
 */
export const Input = ({ 
  type = "text", 
  placeholder, 
  value, 
  onChange, 
  onSubmit, 
  disabled = false, 
  label, 
  className = "" 
}: InputProps) => {
  const [inputValue, setInputValue] = useState(value ?? "");

  useEffect(() => {
    if (value !== undefined) setInputValue(value);
  }, [value]);

  const handleChange = (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    setInputValue(e.target.value);
    onChange?.(e.target.value);
  };

  const handleKeyDown = (e: React.KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.key === "Enter") {
      onSubmit?.(inputValue);
    }
  };

  return (
    <div className="space-y-2">
      {label && (
        <label className="text-sm text-gray-400 block mb-1">{label}</label>
      )}
      <input
        type={type}
        placeholder={placeholder}
        value={inputValue}
        onChange={handleChange}
        onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}
        disabled={disabled}
        className={`
          w-full rounded-md border border-gray-700 bg-gray-900/50 px-3 py-2 text-sm 
          text-white placeholder-gray-500 focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 
          focus:ring-green-500 focus:border-green-500 ${className}
        `}
      />
    </div>
  );
};
"}}

Simulated order entry and portfolio accounting. **No order reaches a broker.** All state
lives in Convex under the authenticated user, and every balance can be rebuilt from the
`paperLedger` table.

The decision logic is pure TypeScript in `convex/paperCore/` (`config.ts`, `engine.ts`), so
the unit tests exercise exactly the code the mutation runs. `convex/paper.ts` is a thin
adapter: load rows → `evaluateOrder` → persist the result in one transaction.

## Order policy

| Rule | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Market buy | Fills at the ask, or the last price if the source has no book |
| Market sell | Fills at the bid, or the last price if the source has no book |
| Limit buy | Fills immediately at that reference price only when reference ≤ limit; otherwise rests as `OPEN` |
| Limit sell | Fills immediately at that reference price only when reference ≥ limit; otherwise rests as `OPEN` |
| Not modelled | Slippage, brokerage, STT, stamp duty, GST, DP charges |
| Rejected outright | Stop-loss orders, indices, derivatives, fractional shares, short selling, margin |

A resting limit is **never** filled by a background job. The simulation has no continuous
feed, so assuming an unobserved tick crossed the limit would be fabricated. `recheckOrder`
re-evaluates it on explicit user action; `cancelOrder` releases its reservation.

## Price eligibility and labels

1. A stored, non-sample `marketQuotes` row i [… 1,031 characters omitted]  `paper.recheckOrder`.
  No mutation accepts a balance.
- **Buys:** cash −= quantity × price; position quantity += quantity; cost basis += the same
  amount. Average cost is `costBasis / quantity`.
- **Partial sells (weighted average):** the removed cost is
  `quantity × (costBasis / quantityHeld)`; the remaining cost basis keeps the same average.
  Realised P&L = proceeds − removed cost. Selling the entire holding removes the position
  row and leaves the ledger entry behind.
- `availableCash` is the account balance. Open **buy** limits reserve `quantity × limit`;
  `spendableCash = availableCash − reservedCash`. Open **sell** limits reserve their shares,
  so the same shares cannot back two orders.
- Equity = cash + market value; total P&L = realised + unrealised.

Replaying `paperLedger` (`replayLedger` in the engine, or the Portfolio table) reproduces
`availableCash` and `realizedPnl` exactly.

## States and idempotency

`(new) → FILLED | OPEN | REJECTED`, `OPEN → FILLED | CANCELLED`.
`FILLED`, `CANCELLED`, `REJECTED` are terminal. Only `FILLED` moves cash or positions;
cancelled and rejected orders stay in the history with their reason.

Each order carries a client-generated `clientOrderId`, unique per account. A retry with the
same reference returns the existing order and writes no second ledger entry. Convex mutations
are transactional, so two concurrent orders that would overspend are serialised: the second is
re-evaluated against the updated balance and rejected.

## Security

- Owner comes from `getAuthUserId`; instrument ids are validated against the catalogue.
- Reading another user's order id returns `Order not found` (no existence leak).
- Signed-out calls return `null` / empty lists for queries and `Not authenticated` for mutations.
- Starting capital can be set only before the first order; afterwards it is locked so past
  performance cannot be rewritten.
- Provider credentials stay in the Convex deployment; the browser receives only env var
  *names* for setup instructions.

## Data presented to the user

All values are virtual. The trading and portfolio views carry a paper-trading notice, and each
position, fill and ledger row shows its data-mode badge. Sample prices are never presented as
provider prices, and simulated returns are never presented as real brokerage performance.

**Backend (Convex)**

## Policies as implemented

Market buys fill at the **ask**, sells at the **bid** (last price when there is no book). Limit orders fill immediately at that same reference price only when it already satisfies the limit, so a fill never breaches it; otherwise they rest as `OPEN`. No background fill loop — `Re-check` is an explicit user action, and `Cancel` releases the reservation. Fees, taxes, slippage, shorting, margin, derivatives and fractional shares are **not** modelled; stop-loss and non-equity instruments are rejected outright.

Accounting is weighted-average: a partial sell removes `quantity × (costBasis / quantityHeld)` and realised P&L is proceeds − removed cost, so the remaining average is unchanged. Open buy limits reserve `quantity × limit`, open sell limits reserve their shares, and `spendableCash = cash − reservedCash`. States are `(new) → FILLED | OPEN | REJECTED`, `OPEN → FILLED | CANCELLED`; only `FILLED` moves money, and cancelled/rejected rows stay in history with a reason.

Every fill stores `fillMode`/`fillSource`/`fillQuoteTime`, sharing the resolver with portfolio valuation. A stored provider quote wins; it is downgraded to `CACHED` when older than 5 minutes, and `HISTORICAL` is never tradable; the sample series is used only while the demo switch is on and is always labelled `SAMPLE`.

# MarketLab — Phase 4: Strategy Builder and Historical Backtesting Engine

Continue from the existing MarketLab repository and `version_1` branch. Preserve the current Convex backend, authentication, stock-card dashboard, instrument details, market-data adapters, paper-trading engine, portfolio, order history, and ledger.

Phase 3 is reported complete with 159 passing tests, a successful build, and browser verification of simulated orders. All currently verified prices and fills are labelled SAMPLE because no market-data provider credentials are configured.

**Objective:** Build a reliable, reproducible strategy builder and historical backtesting engine that lets users define trading rules, test them against historical candle data, and inspect results.

This phase is for historical simulation only. Do not place broker orders, modify live paper-trading accounts, or execute strategies automatically.

## 1. Inspect the existing code first

Review the existing instrument model, normalized candle types, market-data adapters, indicator calculations, paper-trading engine, Convex schema, authentication and ownership checks, and existing test suite.

Reuse existing indicators and calculation utilities where correct. Avoid duplicating the paper-trading accounting model unnecessarily.

Before implementing, identify which historical datasets are available, which are sample-only, and which are genuinely provider-sourced. Do not assume a provider is configured merely because an adapter exists.

## 2. Strategy Builder

Create a dedicated Strategies page that matches MarketLab's dark financial-terminal design.

Users should be able to create, edit, duplicate, save, and delete their own strategies.

Each strategy should have:
- Strategy name and description.
- Instrument or eligible instrument universe.
- Candle interval supported by the selected dataset.
- Backtest start and end dates.
- Initial virtual capital.
- Position-sizing method.
- Entry conditions.
- Exit conditions.
- Optional stop-loss and take-profit rules.
- Trading-cost assumptions.
- Strategy version and creation/update timestamps.

Use a structured rule builder rather than arbitrary executable JavaScript or Python supplied by the user.

Support a focused first set of conditions, such as:
- Price crosses above or below a moving average.
- SMA/EMA comparisons.
- RSI above or below a threshold.
- MACD line/signal crossover when the required data exists.
- Entry and exit conditions combined with AND/OR logic.

Support long-only cash-equity strategies initially. Reject unsupported instruments and invalid rule combinations with clear validation messages.

## 3. Backtesting engine

Implement a deterministic, testable historical simulation engine using normalized OHLCV candles.

Keep the core calculations independent of React and Convex so they can be tested using fixed datasets.

Required capabilities:
- Load a defined historical dataset and interval.
- Calculate indicators without using future observations.
- Generate entry and exit signals.
- Track cash, positions, trades, equity, and drawdown.
- Apply configured position sizing and risk constraints.
- Prevent purchases when available cash is insufficient.
- Prevent selling more shares than the strategy owns.
- Record each simulated trade's signal time, execution time, price, quantity, and reason.
- Calculate a reproducible equity curve.
- Produce a detailed run result and summary metrics.

### Execution rules

Document and implement a consistent execution policy.

For example, if a signal is calculated from a candle's closing price, do not assume the strategy can also execute at that same close unless the simulation explicitly models a valid closing-auction order. Prefer execution on the next eligible candle's open for a conservative, understandable first version.

Account for gaps between candles, unavailable prices, invalid OHLC values, duplicate timestamps, and missing intervals. Do not fabricate candles to make a backtest appear complete.

A stop-loss or take-profit that could both be reached within the same candle has ambiguous execution order. Implement a conservative documented rule or mark the result as ambiguous; never choose the favorable outcome without evidence.

Do not allow future candle data to affect earlier indicators, decisions, position sizing, or fills.

## 4. Trading costs and sizing

Support configurable, clearly documented assumptions for:
- Initial capital.
- Fixed or percentage-based brokerage/transaction costs.
- Slippage in basis points, if enabled.
- Position sizing, such as fixed quantity or a percentage of available equity.
- Maximum position size or exposure.

Use realistic safeguards, but do not claim the default costs exactly reproduce actual Indian exchange, brokerage, tax, or statutory charges.

If actual cost schedules are not configured, identify the costs as user-defined simulation assumptions.

Use consistent INR precision and whole-share quantities for the initial equity-only implementation. Do not add leverage, margin, short selling, derivatives, or fractional shares.

## 5. Prevent look-ahead and data leakage

This is a critical requirement.

- Indicators at a given candle may use only information available at that point.
- Entry signals cannot use future candles.
- Execution cannot use prices that were not available under the selected execution policy.
- Warm-up periods must be respected.
- Missing candles and session boundaries must be handled explicitly.
- Use chronologically sorted, validated data.
- Do not use the final test period to tune strategy parameters automatically.
- Include regression tests that prove future candles cannot change earlier results.

Where a dataset lacks sufficient history or has incomplete coverage, show a clear warning or refuse the run.

## 6. Historical data and sample-mode integrity

Use the existing candle and provider interfaces. Do not introduce a new market-data provider in this phase.

Each backtest run must store:
- Data source and data mode.
- Instrument and candle interval.
- Historical start/end timestamps.
- Dataset identity or version/hash.
- Strategy configuration snapshot.
- Execution and cost assumptions.
- Engine version.
- Creation time and completion status.

Support sample datasets for development, but label results prominently as SAMPLE. Never imply that synthetic or deterministic demo candles are genuine Indian market history.

When genuine provider history is available, use it only if its licensing permits the intended storage and analysis. Do not redistribute restricted historical data.

### Limit orders

A limit buy must never fill above its limit price. A limit sell must never fill below its limit price.

For this initial version:
- Execute immediately only when the currently eligible price satisfies the limit condition.
- Otherwise, leave the order open or reject it with a clear explanation according to the documented order policy.

- Sufficient sellable position quantity for sells.

- Duplicate submissions and repeated execution.
- Valid order-state transitions.
- Concurrent orders attempting to spend the same cash or sell the same shares.
- Consistent cash and position accounting after fills, rejections, and cancellations.

## Policies as implemented

Market buys fill at the **ask**, sells at the **bid** (last price when there is no book). Limit orders fill immediately at that same reference price only when it already satisfies the limit, so a fill never breaches it; otherwise they rest as `OPEN`. No background fill loop — `Re-check` is an explicit user action, and `Cancel` releases the reservation. Fees, taxes, slippage, shorting, margin, derivatives and fractional shares are **not** modelled; stop-loss and non-equity instruments are rejected outright.

Accounting is weighted-average: a partial sell removes `quantity × (costBasis / quantityHeld)` and realised P&L is proceeds − removed cost, so the remaining average is unchanged. Open buy limits reserve `quantity × limit`, open sell limits reserve their shares, and `spendableCash = cash − reservedCash`. States are `(new) → FILLED | OPEN | REJECTED`, `OPEN → FILLED | CANCELLED`; only `FILLED` moves money, and cancelled/rejected rows stay in history with a reason.

                type="date"
                value={dateInputValue(config.fromMs)}
                onChange={(value) => updateConfig({ fromMs: dateInputToMs(value) })}
              />
              <Input
                label="End date"
                type="date"
                value={dateInputValue(config.toMs)}
                onChange={(value) => updateConfig({ toMs: dateInputToMs(value) })}
              />
            </div>

            <div className="mt-3 grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 md:grid-cols-4">
              <NumberField
                label="Initial capital (INR)"
                value={config.initialCapital}
                onChange={(value) => updateConfig({ initialCapital: value ?? 100000 })}
              />
              <Select
                label="Position sizing"
                value={config.sizing.kind}
                onSelect={(value) => updateConfig({ sizing: { ...config.sizing, kind: value as "PERCENT_OF_EQUITY" | "FIXED_QUANTITY" } })}
                options={SIZING}
              />
              {config.sizing.kind === "PERCENT_OF_EQUITY" ? (
                <NumberField
                  label="% of equity per trade"
                  value={config.sizing.percentOfEquity}
                  onChange={(value) => updateConfig({ sizing: { ...config.sizing, percentOfEquity: value } })}
                />
              ) : (
                <NumberField
                  label="Fixed quantity (shares)"
                  value={config.sizing.quantity}
                  onChange={(value) => updateConfig({ sizing: { ...config.sizing, quantity: value } })}
                />
              )}
              <NumberField
                label="Max position % of equity"
                value={config.sizing.maxPositionValuePct}
                onChange={(value) => updateConfig({ sizing: { ...config.sizing, maxPositionValuePct: value } })}
              />
            </div>

            <div className="mt-3 grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 md:grid-cols-4">
              <NumberField
                label="Stop-loss %"
                value={config.stopLossPct}
                onChange={(value) => updateConfig({ stopLossPct: value })}
              />
              <NumberField
                label="Take-profit %"
                value={config.takeProfitPct}
                onChange={(value) => updateConfig({ takeProfitPct: value })}
              />
              <NumberField

                onChange={(value) => updateConfig({ costs: { ...config.costs, brokerageFlat: value ?? 0 } })}

              <NumberField

                value={config.costs.slippageBps}
                onChange={(value) => updateConfig({ costs: { ...config.costs, slippageBps: value ?? 0 } })}
              />
            </div>

            <div className="mt-3 md:w-64">
              <Select
                label="Dataset"
                value={config.datasetMode}
                onSelect={(value) => updateConfig({ datasetMode: value as "AUTO" | "SAMPLE_ONLY" })}
                options={DATASET}
              />

          </Card>

          <div className="mt-4 grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 xl:grid-cols-2">
            <Card>
              <RuleEditor
                title="Entry rules"
                description="Conditions that open a long position when true on the signal candle."
                ruleSet={config.entry}
                onChange={(entry) => updateConfig({ entry })}
                allowEmpty={false}
              />
              {!entryValid && <p className="ml-rule-error">{emptyMessages.entry}</p>}
            </Card>
            <Card>
              <RuleEditor
                title="Exit rules"
                description="Conditions that close the position. Leave empty to rely on stop/take-profit or end-of-data."
                ruleSet={config.exit}
                onChange={(exit) => updateConfig({ exit })}
                allowEmpty
                emptyHint={emptyMessages.exit}
              />
            </Card>
          </div>

            <Card className="mt-4 border-red-500/40">
              <p className="text-sm text-red-200">{runError}</p>

                deterministic result.

                View instrument chart
              </Button>
            </Card>
          )}
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
};

+import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
+import { runBacktest } from "../convex/backtestCore/engine";
+import type { Candle } from "../convex/backtestCore/types";
+
+function makeCandle(ts: number, o: number, h: number, l: number, c: number): Candle {
+  return { ts, open: o, high: h, low: l, close: c, volume: 1000 };
+}
+
+describe("backtest look-ahead prevention", () => {
+  it("does not use future candles to form decisions at earlier bars", () => {
+    const base: Candle[] = [
+      makeCandle(1, 100, 101, 99, 100),
+      makeCandle(2, 100, 101, 99, 100),
+      makeCandle(3, 100, 101, 99, 100),
+      makeCandle(4, 100, 101, 99, 100),
+      makeCandle(5, 100, 105, 99, 104),
+    ];
+    const prefixA = base.slice();
+    const suffixA: Candle[] = [makeCandle(6, 104, 110, 103, 109)];
+    const suffixB: Candle[] = [makeCandle(6, 104, 110, 50, 60)];
+    const padding: Candle[] = [];
+    for (let i = 0; i < 50; i++) padding.push(makeCandle(100 + i, 90, 91, 89, 90));
+
+    const config = {
+      instrumentId: "NSE:TEST:EQUITY",
+      interval: "1d" as const,
+      fromMs: 1,
+      toMs: 1000,
+      initialCapital: 100000,
+      datasetMode: "SAMPLE" as const,
+      sizing: { kind: "PERCENT_OF_EQUITY" as const, quantity: null, percentOfEquity: 100, maxPositionValuePct: 100 },
+      entry: {
+        combinator: "AND" as const,
+        conditions: [{ type: "PRICE_CROSS_ABOVE_MA" as const, maKind: "SMA" as const, period: 3, fast: null, slow: null, signal: null, threshold: null }],
+      },
+      exit: {
+        combinator: "AND" as const,
+        conditions: [{ type: "PRICE_CROSS_BELOW_MA" as const, maKind: "SMA" as const, period: 3, fast: null, slow: null, signal: null, threshold: null }],
+      },
+      stopLossPct: null,
+      takeProfitPct: null,
+      costs: { brokerageFlat: 0, brokeragePct: 0, slippageBps: 0 },
+    };
+
+    const candlesA = prefixA.concat(suffixA).concat(padding);
+    const candlesB = prefixA.concat(suffixB).concat(padding);
+    const dataset = { kind: "sample" as const, source: "sample", mode: "SAMPLE" as const, datasetId: null, hash: "a", rowCount: candlesA.length, firstTs: 1, lastTs: candlesA[candlesA.length-1].ts, gaps: 0, label: "SAMPLE" };
+    const datasetB = { ...dataset, hash: "b", rowCount: candlesB.length };
+
+    const resA = runBacktest({ candles: candlesA, config, dataset });
+    const resB = runBacktest({ candles: candlesB, config, dataset: datasetB });
+
+    expect(resA.trades.length).toBe(resB.trades.length);
+    if (resA.trades.length > 0) {
+      expect(resA.trades[0].entryTs).toBe(resB.trades[0].entryTs);
+      expect(resA.trades[0].entryPrice).toBe(resB.trades[0].entryPrice);
+      expect(resA.trades[0].quantity).toBe(resB.trades[0].quantity);
+    }
+  });
+});

# MarketLab — Phase 4.1: Backtesting Validation, Reliability and Data Integrity

Continue from the existing MarketLab repository and `version_1` branch. Phase 4 is reported complete, with a strategy builder, structured rules, deterministic backtesting engine, Convex persistence, equity/drawdown charts, trade tables, and 193 passing tests.

Do not rebuild the app or add new trading features before validating the engine. The purpose of this phase is to independently verify correctness and fix any defects uncovered.

## 1. Inspect the implementation

Review the actual implementation and tests, particularly:
- The pure backtesting engine and execution policy.
- Existing indicator and candle-normalization utilities.
- Strategy validation and position-sizing rules.
- Stop-loss and take-profit execution.
- Transaction costs and slippage.
- Equity curve, drawdown and performance metric calculations.
- Convex persistence, dataset provenance and ownership checks.
- The Strategies page and result visualizations.

Identify the existing files and tests rather than assuming the previous summary covers every edge case.

## 2. Independent numerical verification

Create small, hand-calculated OHLCV fixtures with known expected results. Calculate expected values independently of the engine under test.

Test:
- Buy and sell signals and next-eligible-candle execution.
- Cash, holdings, trade quantity and final equity.
- Partial exits and multiple consecutive trades.
- Weighted or configured position sizing.
- Brokerage/transaction costs and slippage.
- Stop-loss and take-profit execution.
- Gap-through-stop behavior.
- Ambiguous candles where both stop-loss and take-profit are reachable.
- Trading restrictions when cash or available quantity is insufficient.
- Maximum exposure and position-size limits.
- Zero-trade and single-trade strategies.
- Correct handling of rejected or incomplete runs.

Assert exact values within documented rounding tolerances. Do not merely compare the engine's output against itself or duplicate its implementation in the test.

## 3. Look-ahead bias and execution integrity

Verify that:
- Indicators only use candles available at the time of the signal.
- A signal calculated from candle close cannot execute at that same close under the chosen next-open policy.
- Changing future candles cannot change earlier signals, fills, or equity values.
- Warm-up periods cannot produce premature signals.
- No future high, low, close, or volume is used to decide an earlier trade.
- Missing candles, out-of-order timestamps, duplicate candles, and invalid OHLC relationships are handled explicitly.
- Overnight and session gaps follow the documented execution policy.
- If stop-loss and take-profit could both be reached in one candle, the conservative ambiguity policy is consistently applied.
- Repeated runs with identical inputs produce identical results.

Document any assumptions that cannot be verified from candle data alone.

## 4. Data provenance and sample-mode safeguards

Inspect how each run records its dataset identity, provenance hash, instrument, interval, date range, strategy configuration, engine version and execution assumptions.

Ensure:
- SAMPLE data is visibly and consistently labelled.
- Sample results cannot be mistaken for genuine Indian historical market data.
- The UI never silently replaces unavailable real historical data with sample candles.
- Historical results cannot be described as LIVE.
- Incomplete datasets and unsupported intervals produce warnings or a safe refusal.
- Dataset hashes are calculated over a documented canonical representation and change when the underlying data changes.
- Saved results remain interpretable if the strategy is edited later.
- The original strategy configuration and execution assumptions used for a run are preserved.

Do not claim that a provenance hash proves that a dataset is authentic; it proves identity/integrity only relative to the data hashed.

## 5. Performance metrics audit

Verify the mathematical definitions and edge cases for:
- Net profit and percentage return.
- Realized and unrealized P&L, where applicable.
- Maximum drawdown and the equity peak used as its reference.
- Winning and losing trades.
- Win rate.
- Average win and average loss.
- Profit factor.
- Total transaction costs.
- Exposure/time in market, if implemented.

Avoid misleading annualized returns when date coverage is insufficient. Handle zero losses, no trades, zero initial equity, missing valuations and undefined ratios without `NaN`, infinity or silently fabricated zeros.

Display the formulas or concise definitions in the interface or documentation so users can interpret metrics correctly.

## 6. Security and persistence audit

Using the real development deployment:
- Verify every strategy and saved run is scoped to its authenticated owner.
- Test unauthorized reads, edits and deletions.
- Confirm that users cannot submit arbitrary precomputed results as trusted engine output.
- Validate input sizes, candle-count limits, strategy complexity and execution time.
- Ensure large simulations cannot create unbounded Convex work.
- Check that saved results survive reloads and that editing a strategy does not rewrite the historical snapshot of an earlier run.
- Preserve all existing Phase 1–3 authentication, ownership, ledger and idempotency protections.

Do not weaken access controls to make tests pass.

## 7. UI and browser validation

Verify the full workflow:
1. Create and save a strategy.
2. Configure an instrument, interval, date range, capital and supported rules.
3. Run a backtest.
4. Inspect the equity curve, drawdown, trade markers, trade list and summary metrics.
5. Reload and reopen the saved run.
6. Edit the strategy and confirm the earlier run retains its original configuration snapshot.
7. Try invalid rules and unsupported data ranges.
8. Confirm that all sample-based results are clearly labelled.

Fix any errors that prevent a user from understanding which data and assumptions produced a result.

## 8. Verification

Run and report actual results for:
- `npx convex codegen`
- Convex schema/function validation.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npx vitest run`
- `npx vite build`
- Browser verification against the current development deployment.

Add regression tests for each defect found. Do not report an unexecuted test as passed.

## 9. Deliverable

Provide:

# MarketLab — Phase 4.2: Historical Market-Data Readiness and Integration

Continue from the current MarketLab repository and existing Phase 1–4.1 implementation. Do not restart the project or replace working systems.

## Objective

Make the existing historical market-data pipeline ready for trustworthy backtesting using authorized provider data. Focus on correctness, provenance, safe provider integration, and transparent sample-data behavior.

This phase does NOT implement live trading, broker order placement, or real-money execution.

## 1. Inspect before changing code

Inspect the current provider adapters, market-data functions, candle normalization, storage, backtesting engine, strategies UI, environment configuration, and tests.

Identify:
- Which providers and historical endpoints are actually implemented.
- Which timeframes, exchanges, instruments, and history ranges each provider supports.
- Whether historical candles already flow into the backtesting engine.
- Where SAMPLE data is generated or used as fallback.
- Existing caching, rate limits, pagination, timestamps, and error handling.

Do not claim a provider works unless you can verify its behavior. Preserve existing architecture where practical.

## 2. Historical data adapter

Implement or complete a common historical-candle interface compatible with the existing backtest engine.

Each candle must have a documented, consistent representation of:
- Instrument and exchange identity.
- Candle interval.
- Timestamp and timezone convention.
- Open, high, low, close, and volume.
- Data source and provenance.
- Whether the dataset is SAMPLE or provider-sourced.

Normalize provider responses into this representation. Validate OHLC relationships, finite numeric values, nonnegative volume where applicable, duplicate timestamps, ordering, and invalid or missing fields.

Do not silently fabricate candles, interpolate missing prices, or replace failed provider responses with SAMPLE data while labeling them as historical.

## 3. Time and market-session correctness

Check and test:
- UTC storage or another explicitly documented canonical timezone.
- Correct conversion to Indian market time where needed.
- Candle start/end timestamp conventions.
- Duplicate and out-of-order candles.
- Missing intervals, market holidays, and non-trading periods.
- Partial/incomplete latest candles.
- Daylight-saving and timezone handling for any supported non-Indian markets.

Do not mistake a market closure for missing data. Do not assume every instrument trades in the same session.

## 4. Provider access and limitations

Use the existing authorized adapters. Keep API credentials server-side and never expose secrets in frontend bundles or logs.

If credentials are unavailable:
- Continue with mock fixtures and provider-contract tests.
- Clearly identify which live provider checks could not be completed.
- Do not report live integration as verified.

Respect provider rate limits, terms, data entitlements, and redistribution restrictions. Add bounded pagination, request timeouts, useful errors, and caching where appropriate. Avoid aggressive retries and uncontrolled history downloads.

Do not scrape websites as a substitute for an authorized API.

## 5. Backtest dataset integrity

Ensure a backtest uses one explicit, immutable dataset snapshot. Record:
- Source and SAMPLE/HISTORICAL classification.
- Instrument, exchange, timeframe, and requested date range.
- Actual available date range and candle count.
- Dataset hash based on canonical normalized candle content.
- Strategy/configuration snapshot and engine version, if not already recorded.

A hash proves dataset consistency, not authenticity. Never label a dataset HISTORICAL merely because it has timestamps or a hash.

If the requested range is incomplete or contains unexplained gaps, show a clear warning or reject the run according to a documented policy. Prevent incomplete data from silently producing misleading results.

Ensure that editing or refreshing market data later cannot silently change an already saved run's dataset.

## 6. UI and user-facing behavior

Improve the existing strategy/backtest workflow so users can see:
- Data source and mode.
- Instrument, exchange, timeframe, and date range.
- Actual coverage and candle count.
- Missing-data or validation warnings.
- Whether results are SAMPLE or provider-sourced.

Keep SAMPLE data available for demos, but label it prominently. Never mix SAMPLE and provider candles in one run unless an explicit, documented mode supports that behavior and labels the result unambiguously.

When a provider is not configured or a request fails, explain the issue and preserve a clear retry path without disguising it as successful historical data.

## 7. Security, storage, and resource limits

Verify authentication and per-user ownership on all relevant backend functions. Enforce reasonable maximum date ranges, candle counts, request sizes, and stored dataset/run sizes. Do not trust client-supplied prices, provenance, dataset hashes, or performance results without server-side validation.

- Invalid OHLCV values.

Use deterministic fixtures. Do not make the test suite depend on external API availability.

- No production deployment.

- Do not invent provider capabilities or successful API responses.
- Do not expose or request secrets in chat.

## 2. Paper account

Implement a persistent paper account for each authenticated user.

Requirements:
- Create a default paper account when appropriate, without creating duplicates on repeated page loads.
- Allow the user to configure starting virtual capital before placing the first order.
- Use INR as the initial account currency.
- Track initial capital, available cash, invested cost basis, current market value, realized P&L, unrealized P&L, and total P&L.

- Keep all financial calculations on the trusted backend.

Never present virtual capital or simulated returns as real money or real brokerage-account data.

## 3. Simulated order entry

Support these order types initially:

- Market buy
- Market sell
- Limit buy
- Limit sell

Allow whole-share quantities initially. Validate all inputs on the backend.

Every order should record:
- Unique order ID
- User and paper-account ownership
- Canonical instrument ID, symbol, and exchange
- Side and order type
- Requested quantity and limit price, where applicable
- Execution quantity and execution price, if filled
- Status and timestamps
- Data source/mode used for the fill
- Rejection reason, when applicable

Use clear order states, such as `PENDING`, `OPEN`, `FILLED`, `CANCELLED`, and `REJECTED`, with a documented transition model. Avoid invalid transitions and duplicate execution.

### Market orders

Execute a market order only when the backend has an eligible, valid quote or an explicitly enabled sample quote for the simulation.

- Use a consistent, documented fill-price policy.
- Reject missing, malformed, or ineligible quotes.
- Do not call stale or historical prices `LIVE`.
- Clearly label fills based on sample prices as `SAMPLE`.
- Record the exact price and data mode used for each fill.

### Limit orders

A limit buy must never fill above its limit price. A limit sell must never fill below its limit price.

For this initial version:
- Execute immediately only when the currently eligible price satisfies the limit condition.
- Otherwise, leave the order open or reject it with a clear explanation according to the documented order policy.
- Do not pretend that an unobserved intraday price crossed a limit.
- Do not implement background execution or continuous limit-order monitoring unless the existing infrastructure supports it reliably and the behavior is explicitly tested.

## 4. Financial and risk rules

Implement backend-enforced checks for:
- Positive, valid quantity and price.
- Sufficient available cash for buys.
- Sufficient sellable position quantity for sells.
- Ownership of the paper account and instrument.
- Duplicate submissions and repeated execution.
- Valid order-state transitions.
- Concurrent orders attempting to spend the same cash or sell the same shares.
- Consistent cash and position accounting after fills, rejections, and cancellations.

Use atomic Convex mutations or another appropriate transactional design so two concurrent orders cannot overspend the account or sell the same shares twice.

For this initial version, do not support leverage, short selling, margin, derivatives, options, fractional shares, or real broker orders. Explicitly reject unsupported instrument types rather than silently treating them as equities.

Do not add taxes, brokerage fees, or slippage as if they were exact real-world costs. If simulated fees or slippage are introduced, make the assumptions configurable, explicit, and testable. Otherwise, state that the simulation excludes them.

- Permit sample-based fills only in explicitly enabled development/demo mode.
- Make the chosen mode visible before order submission and in the resulting order history.
- Record a timestamp and the quote source/mode used for every fill.
- Do not silently fall back from a failed provider request to sample prices for an apparently real order.

- A buy reduces cash and increases position quantity and cost basis.
- A sell increases cash and reduces position quantity and cost basis.
- Realized P&L is calculated consistently against the applicable cost basis.
- Unrealized P&L is based on the current eligible valuation price and carries its data-mode label.
- Cancelled and rejected orders do not alter cash or positions.
- Replaying or retrying an order cannot duplicate its ledger entries.
- Account summaries reconcile with the underlying records.

Document how the system handles selling part of a position and how the remaining cost basis is calculated. Use a consistent method, such as weighted-average cost, throughout the application.

Use a structured rule builder rather than arbitrary executable JavaScript or Python supplied by the user.

Support a focused first set of conditions, such as:
- Price crosses above or below a moving average.
- SMA/EMA comparisons.
- RSI above or below a threshold.
- MACD line/signal crossover when the required data exists.
- Entry and exit conditions combined with AND/OR logic.

Support long-only cash-equity strategies initially. Reject unsupported instruments and invalid rule combinations with clear validation messages.

## 3. Backtesting engine

Implement a deterministic, testable historical simulation engine using normalized OHLCV candles.

Keep the core calculations independent of React and Convex so they can be tested using fixed datasets.

Required capabilities:
- Load a defined historical dataset and interval.
- Calculate indicators without using future observations.
- Generate entry and exit signals.
- Track cash, positions, trades, equity, and drawdown.
- Apply configured position sizing and risk constraints.
- Prevent purchases when available cash is insufficient.
- Prevent selling more shares than the strategy owns.
- Record each simulated trade's signal time, execution time, price, quantity, and reason.
- Calculate a reproducible equity curve.
- Produce a detailed run result and summary metrics.

### Execution rules

Document and implement a consistent execution policy.

For example, if a signal is calculated from a candle's closing price, do not assume the strategy can also execute at that same close unless the simulation explicitly models a valid closing-auction order. Prefer execution on the next eligible candle's open for a conservative, understandable first version.

Account for gaps between candles, unavailable prices, invalid OHLC values, duplicate timestamps, and missing intervals. Do not fabricate candles to make a backtest appear complete.

A stop-loss or take-profit that could both be reached within the same candle has ambiguous execution order. Implement a conservative documented rule or mark the result as ambiguous; never choose the favorable outcome without evidence.

Do not allow future candle data to affect earlier indicators, decisions, position sizing, or fills.

## 4. Trading costs and sizing

Support configurable, clearly documented assumptions for:
- Initial capital.
- Fixed or percentage-based brokerage/transaction costs.
- Slippage in basis points, if enabled.
- Position sizing, such as fixed quantity or a percentage of available equity.
- Maximum position size or exposure.

Use realistic safeguards, but do not claim the default costs exactly reproduce actual Indian exchange, brokerage, tax, or statutory charges.

If actual cost schedules are not configured, identify the costs as user-defined simulation assumptions.

Use consistent INR precision and whole-share quantities for the initial equity-only implementation. Do not add leverage, margin, short selling, derivatives, or fractional shares.

## 5. Prevent look-ahead and data leakage

This is a critical requirement.

- Indicators at a given candle may use only information available at that point.
- Entry signals cannot use future candles.
- Execution cannot use prices that were not available under the selected execution policy.
- Warm-up periods must be respected.
- Missing candles and session boundaries must be handled explicitly.
- Use chronologically sorted, validated data.
- Do not use the final test period to tune strategy parameters automatically.
- Include regression tests that prove future candles cannot change earlier results.

## 6. Historical data and sample-mode integrity

Use the existing candle and provider interfaces. Do not introduce a new market-data provider in this phase.

Each backtest run must store:
- Data source and data mode.
- Instrument and candle interval.
- Historical start/end timestamps.
- Dataset identity or version/hash.
- Strategy configuration snapshot.
- Execution and cost assumptions.
- Engine version.
- Creation time and completion status.

Support sample datasets for development, but label results prominently as SAMPLE. Never imply that synthetic or deterministic demo candles are genuine Indian market history.

When genuine provider history is available, use it only if its licensing permits the intended storage and analysis. Do not redistribute restricted historical data.

If there is insufficient genuine historical data, explain why the run cannot be completed rather than silently substituting sample data.

## 7. Results and analytics UI

After a run, display:

- Initial and final equity.
- Net profit/loss and percentage return.
- Maximum drawdown.
- Number of completed trades.
- Winning and losing trades.
- Win rate.
- Average win and average loss.
- Profit factor, when mathematically defined.
- Exposure or time in market, if supported.
- Total modeled transaction costs.

### Visualizations
- Equity curve over time.
- Drawdown curve.
- Historical price chart with entry/exit markers.
- Trade history table.
- Individual trade details.
- Dataset provenance and sample/live-data status.

Handle zero trades, zero losses, missing data, and undefined metrics without `NaN`, infinity, or misleading percentages.

Allow users to save completed run summaries and compare runs they own. Do not persist excessive raw candle copies when a stable permitted dataset reference or hash is sufficient.

## 8. Convex persistence and authorization

Extend the schema only where needed. Support saved strategies and backtest run metadata/results with appropriate indexes.

For every user-specific query and mutation:
- Require authentication.
- Enforce ownership on the backend.
- Validate strategy rules and all numeric parameters.
- Prevent one user from reading, changing, or deleting another user's strategies and runs.
- Do not accept client-provided results as trusted results.
- Keep calculation and result validation on trusted server-side code or a properly isolated computation module.
- Add reasonable limits to run size, candle count, and strategy complexity.
- Prevent arbitrary code execution and unrestricted outbound network requests.

If long-running simulations exceed appropriate Convex execution limits, implement a bounded batch/chunk design or document the architectural limitation. Do not create an unbounded action or claim large-scale backtesting is production-ready without measuring it.

Regenerate official Convex API types and validate the schema using the existing development deployment.

2. Entry and exit rules.
3. Next-candle execution policy.
4. Position sizing and available-cash constraints.
5. Whole-share quantity rules.
6. Brokerage and slippage calculations.

13. Reproducibility for identical inputs.
14. SAMPLE versus genuine historical-data labelling.
15. Invalid strategy rejection.
16. Saved strategy and run persistence.
17. Cross-user authorization and data isolation.
18. Bounded runtime and maximum dataset constraints.
19. Regression tests for the existing paper-trading engine and account ledger.

Do not depend on live markets or external APIs in unit tests.

Review the current schema and existing paper-account, trading, quote, instrument, and authentication code. Reuse existing structures where sound. Avoid duplicating tables, creating competing trading systems, or changing unrelated UI.

Verify the current generated Convex types and test baseline before editing.

## 2. Paper account

Implement a persistent paper account for each authenticated user.

Requirements:
- Create a default paper account when appropriate, without creating duplicates on repeated page loads.
- Allow the user to configure starting virtual capital before placing the first order.
- Use INR as the initial account currency.
- Track initial capital, available cash, invested cost basis, current market value, realized P&L, unrealized P&L, and total P&L.
- Show open positions and an order/trade history.
- Keep all financial calculations on the trusted backend.
- Derive balances from validated account events or transactions, or maintain an auditable ledger. Do not allow client-side balance edits.
- Define consistent rounding and precision rules for currency, quantity, and prices.

Never present virtual capital or simulated returns as real money or real brokerage-account data.

## 3. Simulated order entry

Support these order types initially:

- Market buy
- Market sell
- Limit buy
- Limit sell

Allow whole-share quantities initially. Validate all inputs on the backend.

Every order should record:
- Unique order ID
- User and paper-account ownership
- Canonical instrument ID, symbol, and exchange
- Side and order type
- Requested quantity and limit price, where applicable
- Execution quantity and execution price, if filled
- Status and timestamps
- Data source/mode used for the fill
- Rejection reason, when applicable

Use clear order states, such as `PENDING`, `OPEN`, `FILLED`, `CANCELLED`, and `REJECTED`, with a documented transition model. Avoid invalid transitions and duplicate execution.

### Market orders

Execute a market order only when the backend has an eligible, valid quote or an explicitly enabled sample quote for the simulation.

- Use a consistent, documented fill-price policy.
- Reject missing, malformed, or ineligible quotes.
- Do not call stale or historical prices `LIVE`.
- Clearly label fills based on sample prices as `SAMPLE`.
- Record the exact price and data mode used for each fill.

### Limit orders

A limit buy must never fill above its limit price. A limit sell must never fill below its limit price.

For this initial version:
- Execute immediately only when the currently eligible price satisfies the limit condition.
- Otherwise, leave the order open or reject it with a clear explanation according to the documented order policy.
- Do not pretend that an unobserved intraday price crossed a limit.
- Do not implement background execution or continuous limit-order monitoring unless the existing infrastructure supports it reliably and the behavior is explicitly tested.

## 4. Financial and risk rules

Implement backend-enforced checks for:
- Positive, valid quantity and price.
- Sufficient available cash for buys.
- Sufficient sellable position quantity for sells.
- Ownership of the paper account and instrument.
- Duplicate submissions and repeated execution.
- Valid order-state transitions.
- Concurrent orders attempting to spend the same cash or sell the same shares.
- Consistent cash and position accounting after fills, rejections, and cancellations.

Use atomic Convex mutations or another appropriate transactional design so two concurrent orders cannot overspend the account or sell the same shares twice.

For this initial version, do not support leverage, short selling, margin, derivatives, options, fractional shares, or real broker orders. Explicitly reject unsupported instrument types rather than silently treating them as equities.

Do not add taxes, brokerage fees, or slippage as if they were exact real-world costs. If simulated fees or slippage are introduced, make the assumptions configurable, explicit, and testable. Otherwise, state that the simulation excludes them.

## 5. Quotes and sample-data integrity

- Prefer a valid, sufficiently fresh provider quote when the provider is configured and authorized.
- Permit sample-based fills only in explicitly enabled development/demo mode.
- Make the chosen mode visible before order submission and in the resulting order history.
- Record a timestamp and the quote source/mode used for every fill.
- Do not silently fall back from a failed provider request to sample prices for an apparently real order.
- Do not label sample-derived portfolio performance as live performance.

For each fill, record the cash movement and position movement needed to reconstruct the account. Ensure that:
- A buy reduces cash and increases position quantity and cost basis.
- A sell increases cash and reduces position quantity and cost basis.
- Realized P&L is calculated consistently against the applicable cost basis.
- Unrealized P&L is based on the current eligible valuation price and carries its data-mode label.
- Cancelled and rejected orders do not alter cash or positions.
- Replaying or retrying an order cannot duplicate its ledger entries.
- Account summaries reconcile with the underlying records.

- Current position value

- Verify ownership on the backend.

- Validate instrument IDs, order inputs, and state transitions.

Continue from the existing MarketLab repository and `version_1` branch. Preserve the current Convex backend, authentication, stock-card dashboard, instrument details, market-data adapters, paper-trading engine, portfolio, order history, and ledger.

**Objective:** Build a reliable, reproducible strategy builder and historical backtesting engine that lets users define trading rules, test them against historical candle data, and inspect results.

This phase is for historical simulation only. Do not place broker orders, modify live paper-trading accounts, or execute strategies automatically.

## 1. Inspect the existing code first

Review the existing instrument model, normalized candle types, market-data adapters, indicator calculations, paper-trading engine, Convex schema, authentication and ownership checks, and existing test suite.

Reuse existing indicators and calculation utilities where correct. Avoid duplicating the paper-trading accounting model unnecessarily.

Before implementing, identify which historical datasets are available, which are sample-only, and which are genuinely provider-sourced. Do not assume a provider is configured merely because an adapter exists.

## 2. Strategy Builder

Create a dedicated Strategies page that matches MarketLab's dark financial-terminal design.

Users should be able to create, edit, duplicate, save, and delete their own strategies.

Each strategy should have:
- Strategy name and description.
- Instrument or eligible instrument universe.
- Candle interval supported by the selected dataset.
- Backtest start and end dates.
- Initial virtual capital.
- Position-sizing method.
- Entry conditions.
- Exit conditions.
- Optional stop-loss and take-profit rules.
- Trading-cost assumptions.
- Strategy version and creation/update timestamps.

Use a structured rule builder rather than arbitrary executable JavaScript or Python supplied by the user.

Support a focused first set of conditions, such as:
- Price crosses above or below a moving average.
- SMA/EMA comparisons.
- RSI above or below a threshold.
- MACD line/signal crossover when the required data exists.
- Entry and exit conditions combined with AND/OR logic.

Support long-only cash-equity strategies initially. Reject unsupported instruments and invalid rule combinations with clear validation messages.

## 3. Backtesting engine

Implement a deterministic, testable historical simulation engine using normalized OHLCV candles.

Keep the core calculations independent of React and Convex so they can be tested using fixed datasets.

Required capabilities:
- Load a defined historical dataset and interval.
- Calculate indicators without using future observations.
- Generate entry and exit signals.
- Track cash, positions, trades, equity, and drawdown.
- Apply configured position sizing and risk constraints.
- Prevent purchases when available cash is insufficient.
- Prevent selling more shares than the strategy owns.
- Record each simulated trade's signal time, execution time, price, quantity, and reason.
- Calculate a reproducible equity curve.
- Produce a detailed run result and summary metrics.

### Execution rules

Document and implement a consistent execution policy.

For example, if a signal is calculated from a candle's closing price, do not assume the strategy can also execute at that same close unless the simulation explicitly models a valid closing-auction order. Prefer execution on the next eligible candle's open for a conservative, understandable first version.

Account for gaps between candles, unavailable prices, invalid OHLC values, duplicate timestamps, and missing intervals. Do not fabricate candles to make a backtest appear complete.

A stop-loss or take-profit that could both be reached within the same candle has ambiguous execution order. Implement a conservative documented rule or mark the result as ambiguous; never choose the favorable outcome without evidence.

Do not allow future candle data to affect earlier indicators, decisions, position sizing, or fills.

## 4. Trading costs and sizing

Support configurable, clearly documented assumptions for:
- Initial capital.
- Fixed or percentage-based brokerage/transaction costs.
- Slippage in basis points, if enabled.
- Position sizing, such as fixed quantity or a percentage of available equity.
- Maximum position size or exposure.

Use realistic safeguards, but do not claim the default costs exactly reproduce actual Indian exchange, brokerage, tax, or statutory charges.

If actual cost schedules are not configured, identify the costs as user-defined simulation assumptions.

Use consistent INR precision and whole-share quantities for the initial equity-only implementation. Do not add leverage, margin, short selling, derivatives, or fractional shares.

## 5. Prevent look-ahead and data leakage

This is a critical requirement.

- Indicators at a given candle may use only information available at that point.
- Entry signals cannot use future candles.
- Execution cannot use prices that were not available under the selected execution policy.
- Warm-up periods must be respected.
- Missing candles and session boundaries must be handled explicitly.
- Use chronologically sorted, validated data.
- Do not use the final test period to tune strategy parameters automatically.
- Include regression tests that prove future candles cannot change earlier results.

Where a dataset lacks sufficient history or has incomplete coverage, show a clear warning or refuse the run.

## 6. Historical data and sample-mode integrity

Use the existing candle and provider interfaces. Do not introduce a new market-data provider in this phase.

Each backtest run must store:
- Data source and data mode.
- Instrument and candle interval.
- Historical start/end timestamps.
- Dataset identity or version/hash.
- Strategy configuration snapshot.
- Execution and cost assumptions.
- Engine version.
- Creation time and completion status.

Support sample datasets for development, but label results prominently as SAMPLE. Never imply that synthetic or deterministic demo candles are genuine Indian market history.

When genuine provider history is available, use it only if its licensing permits the intended storage and analysis. Do not redistribute restricted historical data.

If there is insufficient genuine historical data, explain why the run cannot be completed rather than silently substituting sample data.

## 7. Results and analytics UI

- Initial and final equity.
- Net profit/loss and percentage return.
- Maximum drawdown.
- Number of completed trades.
- Winning and losing trades.
- Win rate.
- Average win and average loss.
- Profit factor, when mathematically defined.
- Exposure or time in market, if supported.
- Total modeled transaction costs.

Clearly state that past simulated performance does not predict future returns.

### Visualizations
- Equity curve over time.
- Drawdown curve.
- Historical price chart with entry/exit markers.
- Trade history table.
- Individual trade details.
- Dataset provenance and sample/live-data status.

Handle zero trades, zero losses, missing data, and undefined metrics without `NaN`, infinity, or misleading percentages.

Allow users to save completed run summaries and compare runs they own. Do not persist excessive raw candle copies when a stable permitted dataset reference or hash is sufficient.

Extend the schema only where needed. Support saved strategies and backtest run metadata/results with appropriate indexes.

- Require authentication.
- Enforce ownership on the backend.
- Validate strategy rules and all numeric parameters.
- Prevent one user from reading, changing, or deleting another user's strategies and runs.
- Do not accept client-provided results as trusted results.
- Keep calculation and result validation on trusted server-side code or a properly isolated computation module.
- Add reasonable limits to run size, candle count, and strategy complexity.
- Prevent arbitrary code execution and unrestricted outbound network requests.

If long-running simulations exceed appropriate Convex execution limits, implement a bounded batch/chunk design or document the architectural limitation. Do not create an unbounded action or claim large-scale backtesting is production-ready without measuring it.

2. Entry and exit rules.
3. Next-candle execution policy.
4. Position sizing and available-cash constraints.
5. Whole-share quantity rules.

  config: StrategyConfig,

): ResolvedDataset {
  const candles: BacktestCandle[] = sampleCandles({
    symbol,
    interval: config.interval,
    fromMs: config.fromMs,
    toMs: config.toMs,
  }).map((candle) => ({
    ts: candle.ts,
    open: candle.open,
    high: candle.high,
    low: candle.low,
    close: candle.close,
    volume: candle.volume,
  }));

  const gapInfo = findGaps(candles as any, config.interval);
  const dataset: DatasetInfo = {
    kind: "sample",
    source: "sample",
    mode: "SAMPLE",
    datasetId: null,
    hash: hashCandles(candles),
    rowCount: candles.length,
    firstTs: candles[0]?.ts ?? null,
    lastTs: candles[candles.length - 1]?.ts ?? null,
    gaps: gapInfo.count,
    label: `SAMPLE · deterministic series for ${symbol} (${config.interval}) — ${note}`,
  };

  if (candles.length < MIN_BACKTEST_CANDLES) {
    throw new Error(
      `Only ${candles.length} sample candles fall in the selected range; at least ${MIN_BACKTEST_CANDLES} are needed. Widen the date range.`

 * The single place that decides what a candle request shows when no genuine
 * provider data is available.
 *
 * Everything produced here is labelled `SAMPLE` and names its reason. There is
 * deliberately no code path that relabels sample candles as `HISTORICAL` or a
 * provider source, so a failed provider request can never be presented as real
 * market history.
 */

import { findGaps } from "./normalize";
import { sampleCandles } from "./sample";
import type { Interval, NormalizedCandle, NormalizedInstrument } from "./types";

export interface SampleCandleResult {
  instrumentId: string;
  symbol: string;
  interval: Interval;
  candles: NormalizedCandle[];
  mode: "SAMPLE";
  source: "sample";
  adjusted: NormalizedCandle["adjusted"];
  fetchedAt: number;
  note: string | null;
  warning: string | null;
  quality: {
    rowCount: number;
    gaps: number;
    gapSamples: number[];
    firstTs: number | null;
    lastTs: number | null;
    fromCache: boolean;
  };
}

/** Builds a deterministic SAMPLE candle series with an explicit quality report. */
export function sampleCandleFallback(input: {
  instrument: Pick<NormalizedInstrument, "instrumentId" | "symbol">;
  interval: Interval;
  fromMs: number;
  toMs: number;
  nowMs: number;
  maxCandles: number;
}): SampleCandleResult {
  const candles: NormalizedCandle[] = sampleCandles({
    symbol: input.instrument.symbol,
    interval: input.interval,
    fromMs: input.fromMs,
    toMs: input.toMs,
  })
    .slice(-input.maxCandles)
    .map((candle) => ({
      ...candle,
      instrumentId: input.instrument.instrumentId,
      source: "sample" as const,
      mode: "SAMPLE" as const,
    }));

  const gaps = findGaps(candles, input.interval);
  return {
    instrumentId: input.instrument.instrumentId,
    symbol: input.instrument.symbol,
    interval: input.interval,
    candles,
    mode: "SAMPLE",
    source: "sample",
    adjusted: "unknown",
    fetchedAt: input.nowMs,
    note: null,
    warning: null,
    quality: {
      rowCount: candles.length,
      gaps: gaps.count,
      gapSamples: gaps.firstFew,
      firstTs: candles[0]?.ts ?? null,
      lastTs: candles[candles.length - 1]?.ts ?? null,
      fromCache: false,
    },
  };
}

/**
 * Warning shown when a configured provider failed or returned nothing. The
 * redacted provider message is preserved so the user knows why the chart is
 * synthetic instead of guessing.
 */
export function providerFallbackWarning(providerLabel: string, message: string): string {
  const detail = message.trim() || "no response";
  return `${providerLabel} did not return candles (${detail}). Showing labelled sample data — this is not market history.`;
}

/** Note shown when sample candles are served without any provider being tried. */
export function noProviderNote(input: {
  signedIn: boolean;
  providerLabel: string | null;
  interval: Interval;
}): string {
  if (!input.signedIn) {
    return "Sign in and configure a provider to load real candles — this series is sample data.";
  }
  if (input.providerLabel) {
    return `${input.providerLabel} returned no candles for this range — showing sample data.`;
  }
  return `No configured provider serves ${input.interval} candles — showing sample data.`;
}

{"kind":"tool","id":"iU5qcHNvu2c","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"marketlab/convex/alertsCore.ts","instructions":"Add pure, testable alert evaluation rules that the Convex action will use.","content":"/**
 * Pure rules for evaluating price alerts.
 *
 * The Convex action in `convex/alerts.ts` fetches quotes and persists the
 * outcome; everything that decides *whether* an alert may fire lives here so it
 * can be tested without a deployment or a network.
 *
 * Integrity rules encoded below:
 *  - Only ACTIVE alerts are evaluated. Paused and triggered alerts are left
 *    untouched, so repeated "check now" presses cannot re-trigger history.
 *  - A quote must carry a real price to be considered at all.
 *  - Only LIVE, DELAYED and SAMPLE quotes may cross a threshold. A stale CACHED
 *    or historical series is recorded for display with its own label but can
 *    never fire, so a frozen price cannot masquerade as a market move.
 *  - SAMPLE crossings are counted separately, so the UI can say plainly that a
 *    demo price satisfied the condition.
 */

import type { DataMode } from "./market/types";

export type AlertDirection = "ABOVE" | "BELOW";
export type AlertStatus = "ACTIVE" | "PAUSED" | "TRIGGERED";

/** Modes that are allowed to satisfy an alert threshold. */
export const TRIGGERABLE_MODES: DataMode[] = ["LIVE", "DELAYED", "SAMPLE"];

export function isTriggerableMode(mode: DataMode): boolean {
  return TRIGGERABLE_MODES.includes(mode);
}

/** Inclusive comparison, matching `isAlertConditionMet [… 45 characters omitted]  thresholdMet(
  direction: AlertDirection,
  threshold: number,
  price: number
): boolean {
  if (!Number.isFinite(price) || !Number.isFinite(threshold)) return false;
  return direction === "ABOVE" ? price >= threshold : price <= threshold;
}

export interface EvaluatableAlert<IdType extends string = string> {
  _id: IdType;
  instrumentId: string;
  direction: AlertDirection;
  threshold: number;
  status: AlertStatus;
}

export interface EvaluatableQuote {
  lastPrice: number;
  mode: DataMode;
  source: string;
}

export interface AlertObservation<IdType extends string = string> {
  alertId: IdType;
  price: number;
  mode: DataMode;
  source: string;
  crossed: boolean;
}

export interface AlertEvaluationPlan<IdType extends string = string> {
  observations: AlertObservation<IdType>[];
  /** Alerts skipped because no usable price was available. */
  skippedNoPrice: number;
  /** Alerts whose only price was a stale or historical label; never triggered. */
  skippedStale: number;
  /** Alerts evaluated against a SAMPLE price. */
  sampleEvaluated: number;
  /** SAMPLE evaluations that satisfied the threshold. */
  sampleCrossed: number;
}

export function planAlertEvaluation<IdType extends string>(
  alerts: EvaluatableAlert<IdType>[],
  quotesByInstrument: Map<string, EvaluatableQuote>
): AlertEvaluationPlan<IdType> {
  const plan: AlertEvaluationPlan<IdType> = {
    observations: [],
    skippedNoPrice: 0,
    skippedStale: 0,
    sampleEvaluated: 0,
    sampleCrossed: 0,
  };

  for (const alert of alerts) {
    if (alert.status !== "ACTIVE") continue;

    const quote = quotesByInstrument.get(alert.instrumentId);
    if (!quote || !Number.isFinite(quote.lastPrice) || quote.lastPrice <= 0) {
      plan.skippedNoPrice += 1;
      continue;
    }

    const triggerable = isTriggerableMode(quote.mode);
    if (!triggerable) plan.skippedStale += 1;

    const crossed = triggerable && thresholdMet(alert.direction, alert.threshold, quote.lastPrice);

    if (quote.mode === "SAMPLE") {
      plan.sampleEvaluated += 1;
      if (crossed) plan.sampleCrossed += 1;
    }

    plan.observations.push({
      alertId: alert._id,
      price: quote.lastPrice,
      mode: quote.mode,
      source: quote.source,
      crossed,
    });
  }

  return plan;
}

[candleFallback.test.ts](marketlab/tests/candleFallback.test.ts) (12 tests) pins the contract: result mode is always `SAMPLE` with source `sample`, never `HISTORICAL`/`LIVE`/a provider id, the series is deterministic and capped, the provider's redacted message survives while the text states the data is not market history, and the three "no provider" notes are distinct and all say sample.

**2. Alert integrity — rules extracted, plus a real integrity fix**
New [alertsCore.ts](marketlab/convex/alertsCore.ts) holds the evaluation rules and `alerts.evaluate` now uses it, including a fix: only `LIVE`, `DELAYED` and `SAMPLE` quotes may satisfy a threshold. A `CACHED` or `HISTORICAL` price is recorded on the row with its label but can never fire, and a new `skippedStale` count is surfaced on the Alerts page. [alertIntegrity.test.ts](marketlab/tests/alertIntegrity.test.ts) (13 tests) covers active/paused/triggered gating, re-arm, no duplicate trigger, unusable prices, cross-instrument isolation, SAMPLE marking, and that the backend comparison matches the UI helper at every boundary.

**3. Paper and backtest integrity — extended regression coverage**
[phase7Integrity.test.ts](marketlab/tests/phase7Integrity.test.ts) (11 tests): exact-cash buy settles at zero rather than negative, one rupee short rejects with no side effect, sells never exceed the held or unreserved quantity, a resting limit order moves no cash/position while reserving its worst case, and backtest `inputHash` is stable for identical inputs but changes with costs or sizing.

**4. Defect fixed: the Screener listed quote-less instruments as matches**
It returned 15 rows with every price cell `—` while claiming "15 of 15 evaluated", and its advice to "load quotes on Markets" didn't actually populate stored quotes here. Unquoted instruments are now priced from the same audited deterministic SAMPLE series, every row is labelled `SAMPLE`/`sample`, and a new `samplePriced` count renders as "N rows priced from the deterministic SAMPLE series — no provider quote is stored for those instruments." Preset hints and the zero-match message were corrected too ([screener.ts](marketlab/convex/screener.ts), [Screener.tsx](marketlab/src/pages/Screener.tsx), [marketClient.ts](marketlab/src/lib/marketClient.ts)).
